title: Rectangular prism
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Draw the first face of the rectangular prism by creating the first loop consisting of four lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.021, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.021, 0.0) and ends at (0.021, 0.75). The third line starts at (0.021, 0.75) and ends at (0.0, 0.75). The fourth line completes the loop by starting at (0.0, 0.75) and ending at the origin (0.0, 0.0). Scale the two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.75. Transform the scaled sketch into three dimensions by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it with a vector set to zero. Extrude the sketch 0.021 units along the normal direction without extruding in the opposite direction. Define a boolean operation to create a new solid body from this extrusion. The final dimensions of the part are a length of 0.02096273291925466 units, a width of 0.7499999999999999 units, and a height of 0.020962732919254656 units. The final shape is a rectangular prism with a flat top and bottom, appearing as a straight line in all views.

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.021, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.021, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.021)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · 1 sample
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.021) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.021) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.021)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
